bugs.name: Apply Patch commits an empty file when the pasted diff has a new-file header but no hunk
bugs.summary: The patch is applied and committed without any error: the commit "agent4: broken patch" reports "1 changed files with 0 additions and 0 deletions" and creates agent4-broken.md with 0 B ("The file is empty."). The line of content the user pasted was silently thrown away. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/_diffpatch/agent4-patchtmp)
bugs.expected: Either the content below the +++ line is kept in the file, or the patch is refused with an error (an empty diff / "No valid patches in input"), as happens with a patch that has no diff header at all. It should not commit an empty file while the page shows success for a patch that carries content.
bugs.actual: The patch is applied and committed without any error: the commit "agent4: broken patch" reports "1 changed files with 0 additions and 0 deletions" and creates agent4-broken.md with 0 B ("The file is empty."). The line of content the user pasted was silently thrown away.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval (momentic-eval-1) and open https://5503-imhfwk4zvki4x702wdb5s.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/_diffpatch/agent4-patchtmp/ (any branch you can commit to).
Paste this into the patch editor: 'diff --git a/agent4-broken.md b/agent4-broken.md', 'new file mode 100644', '--- /dev/null', '+++ b/agent4-broken.md', 'this hunk has no @@ header and no + markers'.
Type commit message 'agent4: broken patch' and press "Commit Changes".

The page goes to the commit page /eval/harbor-handbook/commit/c981e2b5919300322e46e8f5600fe615da3a2a68: it shows '1 changed files with 0 additions and 0 deletions' and the new file agent4-broken.md with 0 B; open the file and it says 'The file is empty.'
bugs.reason: Gitea hands the text to git apply (patch.go:163) and git itself accepts this input as a valid empty-file creation, ignoring the trailing non-diff line (reproduced locally with the same flags: exit 0, empty file added). The input was a deliberately malformed patch and the app did what git does with it.

bugs.name: Archive download for a non-existent tag answers a plain-text 404 "unrecognized repository reference"
bugs.summary: The address answers 404 with a bare unstyled white page showing only the raw git message "unrecognized repository reference: no-such-tag" — no site navigation, no repository header, no wording a visitor understands and no way back. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/archive/no-such-tag.zip)
bugs.expected: A clear error page inside the site's layout, e.g. "404 Not Found — the tag no-such-tag does not exist", with navigation and a link back to the repository.
bugs.actual: The address answers 404 with a bare unstyled white page showing only the raw git message "unrecognized repository reference: no-such-tag" — no site navigation, no repository header, no wording a visitor understands and no way back.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1.
Open https://5503-imhfwk4zvki4x702wdb5s.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/tags and note the v1.0.0 row's ZIP link (/eval/harbor-handbook/archive/v1.0.0.zip).

Change the tag in that address to one that does not exist: https://5503-imhfwk4zvki4x702wdb5s.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/archive/no-such-tag.zip (a stale bookmark or a deleted tag gives the same address).
Look at the page that comes back, and reload it.
bugs.reason: Deliberate: the download handler explicitly answers this case with ctx.HTTPError(404, err.Error()), a plain-text reply for a file-download endpoint; the text is Gitea's own RepoRefNotFoundError message, not a raw git error, and the status is a correct 404.

bugs.name: Commit search results do not show the tag badge that the plain commit list shows
bugs.summary: In the search results the row for 4ff25d14a0 shows only the message 'Add engineering handbook and release checklist', without the 'v1.0.0' tag badge that is shown for the identical row in the unfiltered commit list. The badge is missing for every result row, in both 'This Branch' and 'All Branches' searches. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/commits/branch/docs/release-owners/search?q=release)
bugs.expected: The same commit is shown with the same data in both views, including the 'v1.0.0' tag badge that marks it in the branch history.
bugs.actual: In the search results the row for 4ff25d14a0 shows only the message 'Add engineering handbook and release checklist', without the 'v1.0.0' tag badge that is shown for the identical row in the unfiltered commit list. The badge is missing for every result row, in both 'This Branch' and 'All Branches' searches.
reproSteps: Open the commit history of the branch docs/release-owners (/eval/harbor-handbook/commits/branch/docs/release-owners) and look at the last row: commit 4ff25d14a0 'Add engineering handbook and release checklist' carries the tag badge 'v1.0.0'.
Type 'release' in the 'Search commits...' box and submit (the page goes to /commits/branch/docs/release-owners/search?q=release).
Look at the row for the same commit 4ff25d14a0 in the search results.
bugs.reason: Not a defect but a missing extra: tag badges are loaded only by the plain commit list handler (commit.go:95-100) and the shared template shows them only when present; the search view shows no wrong data, it just lacks the decoration (file history lacks it too).

bugs.name: Delete page renders the delete form for a file path that does not exist
bugs.summary: A fully working 'Commit Changes' form is rendered: commit message prefilled 'Delete agent4-does-not-exist.md', the branch radios and an active 'Commit Changes' button. Nothing on the page says the file is missing; only after clicking 'Commit Changes' does the page answer 'The file being deleted, \"agent4-does-not-exist.md\", no longer exists in this repository.' while still showing the same form. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/_delete/main/agent4-does-not-exist.md)
bugs.expected: The page should say that the file does not exist (the repository file view of a missing path answers '404 Not Found — Path agent4-does-not-exist.md doesn't exist in branch/main') instead of offering a delete form for it
bugs.actual: A fully working 'Commit Changes' form is rendered: commit message prefilled 'Delete agent4-does-not-exist.md', the branch radios and an active 'Commit Changes' button. Nothing on the page says the file is missing; only after clicking 'Commit Changes' does the page answer 'The file being deleted, \"agent4-does-not-exist.md\", no longer exists in this repository.' while still showing the same form.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open https://5503-if6f6j5z691kuklo2xtor.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/_delete/main/agent4-does-not-exist.md (a path that does not exist in the repository)
Read the page: it is the normal delete-file form with the message 'Delete agent4-does-not-exist.md' and a 'Commit Changes' button
Compare with the same missing path in the file view: https://5503-if6f6j5z691kuklo2xtor.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/src/branch/main/agent4-does-not-exist.md answers '404 Not Found'
Click 'Commit Changes' to see that the app only then complains that the file no longer exists

bugs.name: Apply Patch answers "The file contents have changed since you started editing" on the first Commit Changes click
bugs.summary: The page reloads on /eval/harbor-handbook/_diffpatch/main with the red banner 'The file contents have changed since you started editing. Click here to see them or Commit Changes again to overwrite them.' Nothing is applied and no commit is created. The same banner appears with garbage text in the editor ('this is not a patch at all') instead of any patch-format error. The response is HTTP 200 and the editor keeps the patch content, but the 'Commit Changes' button comes back disabled, so the suggested 'Commit Changes again' cannot be clicked. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/_diffpatch/main/)
bugs.expected: The patch is applied: the page goes to the repository file view (or the commit) and the new file agent3-patch-test.md exists, with a new commit. No conflict warning, because no file was open for editing and nothing changed on the branch in between.
bugs.actual: The page reloads on /eval/harbor-handbook/_diffpatch/main with the red banner 'The file contents have changed since you started editing. Click here to see them or Commit Changes again to overwrite them.' Nothing is applied and no commit is created. The same banner appears with garbage text in the editor ('this is not a patch at all') instead of any patch-format error. The response is HTTP 200 and the editor keeps the patch content, but the 'Commit Changes' button comes back disabled, so the suggested 'Commit Changes again' cannot be clicked.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open https://5503-i444yii8nkb433ro2trba.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/_diffpatch/main/

Click into the patch editor (line 1) and paste a valid git-style diff that adds a new file: 'diff --git a/agent3-patch-test.md b/agent3-patch-test.md', 'new file mode 100644', '--- /dev/null', '+++ b/agent3-patch-test.md', '@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@', '+# agent3 patch test', '+', '+Created via Apply Patch by agent3.'
In the commit summary field under 'Commit Changes' type agent3-valid-patch
Click the 'Commit Changes' button
bugs.reason: Per source this banner appears only when the branch head differs from the commit recorded when the page was opened (patch.go:143-158); the target was main, which other agents of the same run were pushing to (run3-06's last frame shows a fresh foreign commit on main), so the "false" conflict is most likely a shared-environment artifact, and the evidence does not show otherwise. A human should repeat it on a branch nobody else touches: (a) if the first click still fails, accept as stated; (b) check the finding's second claim, that after this error the Commit Changes button is disabled although the banner says "Commit Changes again" - source supports it (PageHasPosted is set only in the file editor, editor.go:225, never in patch.go) but no screenshot shows the button; if confirmed, accept that narrower bug with severity 3.

bugs.summary: The docs/release-owners row credits commit 698207d676 to user \"eval\": it shows the avatar /avatars/51965088c5db83c3fd307f308d25198a (title \"eval\") and the name \"eval\" linking to /eval. bugs.expected: The author shown next to the branch's latest commit is the same person everywhere: Alex Rivera, as on the commit page /eval/harbor-handbook/commit/698207d676ddae410c422cf90f785f0b8d04bb14 and in the branch history /eval/harbor-handbook/commits/branch/docs/release-owners.
bugs.actual: The docs/release-owners row credits commit 698207d676 to user \"eval\": it shows the avatar /avatars/51965088c5db83c3fd307f308d25198a (title \"eval\") and the name \"eval\" linking to /eval. The commit page of 698207d676 and the branch's own commit history both show the author as \"Alex Rivera\" (avatar daf006c44fe290681b00919b90ff875c). The same commit therefore has two different authors on two pages.
reproSteps: Open https://5503-i444yii8nkb433ro2trba.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/branches (signed in as eval).

Read the "docs/release-owners" row of the Branches list: it shows commit 698207d676, the message "Document release captain and verification responsibilities", "Updated last year" and then the author avatar with the name "eval" (linking to /eval).

bugs.name: Code search for a term starting with "-" ("-i") returns lines that do not contain it
bugs.summary: The search returns every line of every file in the repository (README.md lines 1-9 with the empty lines, docs/contributing.md 1-6, docs/releases.md 1-6, the agent12 files), i.e. the term is consumed as a git grep option instead of being searched as text. Related, the query --name-only answers "No matching results found." instead of being searched literally. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/search)
bugs.expected: The Exact search finds the text "-i" literally. No file in the repository contains "-i" (I checked README.md, docs/contributing.md, docs/releases.md), so the correct answer is the no-results state, as it is for any other absent text.
bugs.actual: The search returns every line of every file in the repository (README.md lines 1-9 with the empty lines, docs/contributing.md 1-6, docs/releases.md 1-6, the agent12 files), i.e. the term is consumed as a git grep option instead of being searched as text. Related, the query --name-only answers "No matching results found." instead of being searched literally.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1.
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/search (search type is "Exact").
Type -i in the "Search code..." box and press Enter (or click Search).
Read the results: README.md lines 1-9 (including the blank lines 2, 4, 7), agent12-x.md line 1, agent12-finder-test.md line 1, docs/contributing.md lines 1-6, docs/releases.md lines 1-6.
Repeat the same search: /eval/harbor-handbook/search?q=-i&search_mode=exact gives the same full-repo listing.
Also try /eval/harbor-handbook/search?q=--name-only&search_mode=exact, which answers "No matching results found."
bugs.reason: The stated cause is wrong and the behaviour is coded on purpose: the term is always passed with -e and its leading dashes are stripped first (grep.go:68: strings.TrimLeft(search, "-")), so "-i" is searched as "i" and "--name-only" as "name-only"; nothing is parsed as a git option, and the blank lines in the result are context lines. Results are a superset of the literal matches, never missing any.
